title: Quantization-aware wide from-scratch trunk: spend the 4 MiB byte budget on raw INT8 capacity instead of ImageNet transfer
hypothesis: 24 straight post-champion rounds (36-59) have tried almost every decode/decision-mechanism family this problem admits -- flat/factorized/coordinate-generated/coarse-to-fine classification fields, retrieve-then-rerank, spatial and lighting dispatchers (three separate attempts: 30, 46, 50, plus this round's immediate predecessor 59's fully-independent twin trunks, 2134.12 m), continuous GMM regression, residual VQ location coding, dense per-patch consensus with two different poolers (attention-mean and IRLS), and two flavors of pixel-reconstruction canonicalization -- and every one of them lost, most by a wide margin. Exactly two rounds instead touched the TRUNK's identity: exp 41/42 (domain-native contrastive pretraining on a from-scratch trunk, the single closest result of the entire losing streak at 846.42 m, +14%) and exp 53 (a different ImageNet-pretrained family, ShuffleNetV2, bundled with a FiLM+top-K decode rewrite, 1552.08 m, worse). Those two data points are the whole project's only real evidence on trunk identity, and they point the same direction every falsification fork since exp 39 has speculated about but never tested: descriptor/trunk capacity, not decode topology, is the wall -- yet no experiment has ever actually varied capacity independent of everything else, because every from-scratch trunk tried so far stored its weights in FP32, which caps raw parameter count at roughly what the champion's compact 190k-param pretrained trunk already has once the field head's own weights (the single biggest tensor in the whole model -- ~570k params, ~2.2 MiB, larger than the trunk itself) are subtracted from the same 4 MiB envelope. CLAUDE.md SS3 names quantization-aware training as an explicit, still-open axis, and the one experiment that used the word 'quantization' (exp 51, residual VQ) tested something categorically different -- quantizing WHERE a location is coded, not HOW MANY BITS each weight costs -- so this axis is genuinely untested, not refuted. This design tests it directly: an from-scratch trunk trained with real quantization-aware weight fake-quantization (straight-through-estimator INT8 rounding baked into every forward pass throughout training, not a post-hoc calibration pass) can be built ~4x wider in raw parameter count than any FP32 from-scratch trunk this project has ever fielded, because INT8 storage is ~4x denser than FP32 -- while still fitting the SAME 4 MiB envelope, once the field head is also quantized. This is a genuine whole-pipeline pivot forced by that one mechanism, not a decode rewrite wearing a pivot's clothes: with no pretrained trunk left to fine-tune gently (the champion's differential trunk/head learning-rate split existed only to protect transferred features, which no longer exist), the champion's two-full-head brightness gate (its single most distinctive satellite mechanism, unchanged since exp 12 and reused by every dispatcher attempt including 30/46/50/59) is also replaced outright by continuous FiLM conditioning of the trunk's own feature map -- a single field head instead of two blended ones, freeing more of the byte budget for trunk width rather than a second redundant head, and testing the never-tried 'unified continuous conditioning' point on CLAUDE.md SS3's unified-vs-dispatcher axis rather than another discrete blend.
method: Replace the ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV3-Small trunk (model/model.py, banned this round) with a from-scratch 5-stage conv trunk (~700k-1.0M conv params, ~4-5x the raw parameter count of any prior from-scratch trunk in this project's history) built entirely from two new QAT wrapper modules (QATConv2d, QATLinear) that fake-quantize their own weight tensor to INT8 (per-output-channel symmetric, straight-through estimator) on every forward call during training, so the network is optimized against real quantization noise from step 1 -- not calibrated after the fact. Brightness conditioning moves from the champion's two-full-head sigmoid-gated blend to continuous FiLM modulation (gamma/beta from a tiny MLP on raw mean luminance) applied to the trunk's own feature map before a SINGLE field head. After training, every QAT-wrapped weight is snapped in-place to its quantized value and the model is exported to FP32 ONNX as before, then immediately repacked by onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic (weight-only INT8, Conv/MatMul/Gemm) into the final shipped `{area}.onnx` -- the real byte-compression step that lets the wider trunk plus the (also quantized) 1024-way field head fit the same 4 MiB gate the champion fits today.
expected_outcome: If raw descriptor capacity really is the dominant wall the last 24 rounds jointly point at (the theory every capacity-adjacent falsification fork since exp 39 has proposed but none has isolated), worst-case median error should land materially below exp 42's 846.42 m -- the best any trunk swap has managed -- targeting roughly 600-800 m, potentially challenging the champion's 743.07 m itself, since this is the first from-scratch trunk with genuinely more raw parameters than the banned pretrained one rather than a parameter-matched substitute. Mechanism-level signature to check post-hoc: training loss should descend smoothly and comparably to champion's own curve shape (confirming the STE fake-quantization noise is not destabilizing optimization), and the final int8 onnx_bytes (logged in train_info.json) should land safely under MODEL_MAX_BYTES (4,194,304) with meaningful margin (targeting ~2.2-3.2 MiB used), confirming the capacity headroom was real and not eaten by quantization/graph overhead. Falsification forks: (a) if training is smooth and the int8 budget check passes with healthy margin, but the primary metric does not clear 846.42 m, the capacity hypothesis is now genuinely refuted for the first time (distinct from 24 rounds of decode churn that never isolated it) -- descriptor byte-width was never the wall, and future rounds should stop treating 'maybe it's capacity' as a live fallback and look instead at the training OBJECTIVE the trunk is taught (contrastive/reconstruction, per exp 41-44's still-open thread) independent of its size; (b) if training loss is visibly noisy/unstable relative to champion's curve (large per-step loss variance, no clean descent), the STE fake-quantization itself -- not the capacity idea -- is the failure mode, and a follow-up should either widen the quantization step's numerical margin (fewer effective bits, e.g. INT8 with a wider clip percentile) or delay fake-quant activation for a short float warm-up before concluding the capacity bet is dead; (c) if the exported int8 model exceeds or barely clears the 4 MiB gate, the field head (not the trunk) ate most of the freed budget, arguing for a coarser field or a smaller trunk-to-head capacity ratio next round rather than abandoning quantization-aware training itself.
eli5: Every recent experiment has tried a cleverer way to make the model's final guess, while quietly keeping the 'brain' behind that guess roughly the same size as before. This experiment instead asks a totally different question: what if the ban on today's champion brain was actually forcing every replacement to be small, because the model has to fit in a fixed amount of memory (like a phone with a small storage card), and a brand-new brain stored the normal way takes up as much room as the champion's whole hard-won head start? So this time we store the new brain's numbers in a more compact format -- like writing prices as '$5' instead of '$5.0000000' -- which lets us build a brain roughly four times bigger inside the exact same memory card, and we train it from day one already knowing it'll be stored that compact way, so it doesn't get confused by the rounding later. We also swap out the old 'is it bright or dark outside' switch (which ran two full separate mini-brains and blended their guesses) for one brain that just continuously dials its own attention up or down based on brightness, freeing up even more room for size.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128x128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: brand-new from-scratch 5-stage conv trunk (stem 3->32 + four stride-2/stride-1 stages up to ~224 channels, 8x8 output), every Conv2d built as a QATConv2d that fake-quantizes its own weight to INT8 (per-output-channel, straight-through estimator) on every forward pass throughout training -- roughly 4-5x the raw parameter count of any prior from-scratch trunk in this project because INT8 storage is ~4x denser than the FP32 every earlier from-scratch attempt used

stages.name: Lighting-conditioned modulation
stages.detail: replaces the champion's two-full-head brightness gate: a tiny MLP reads the crop's own raw-pixel mean luminance and outputs a continuous per-channel scale+shift (FiLM) applied directly to the trunk's own feature map, so lighting conditioning happens once, continuously, inside the shared descriptor -- not as a discrete blend of two separately-scored fields

stages.name: Layout summary
stages.detail: 1x1 QATConv2d squeeze of the (now 224-channel) feature map to a small layout code, flattened and concatenated with the GAP descriptor -- same spirit as the champion's layout code but re-derived for the new channel count and the FiLM-modulated feature map feeding it

stages.name: Probability map
stages.detail: a SINGLE QATLinear field head (no second 'dark expert' head, no gate blend) reads [GAP descriptor + layout code] into 32x32=1024 map-cell logits

stages.name: Rotation ensemble
stages.detail: the crop and its three 90-degree pixel rotations still all pass through the same trunk/head (C4 vote), but the four views' logit maps are now combined by a confidence-weighted average (each view weighted by its own sharpened-field peak mass) instead of the champion's plain unweighted mean, since the four views are not equally trustworthy after a single unified head replaces the two-expert blend

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: same proven soft-argmax read-out as champion (beta-sharpened softmax over the field, expected-coordinate decode, plus the unsharpened-vs-sharpened decode gap) -- this formula has never been implicated in any of the 24 failed rounds, so it is kept, but it now runs on genuinely different (quantized, FiLM-conditioned, single-head, confidence-weighted-ensemble) logits

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: same design intent as champion (calibrated hit-predictor over peak mass, field entropy, sharpened/unsharpened decode gap, detached GAP descriptor, conf_shift buffer) but rebuilt for the new 224-d descriptor and QATLinear layers

stages.name: Deployment quantization
stages.detail: after training, every QAT-wrapped weight is snapped in-place to its quantized value, the model is exported to a clean FP32 ONNX graph (no fake-quant ops baked in), then onnxruntime.quantization.quantize_dynamic repacks Conv/MatMul/Gemm weights into real INT8 storage for the shipped {area}.onnx -- the mechanical step that actually realizes the ~4x byte saving the QAT training prepared the network for

stages.name: Training data
stages.detail: exp-35's confusability-weighted place sampler, unchanged mechanism and unchanged constants (CONFUSABILITY_ALPHA, NEIGHBOR_EXCLUDE_R) -- this experiment's variable is trunk precision/capacity and the lighting-conditioning mechanism, not the sampler

stages.name: Training procedure
stages.detail: single Adam param group over all model parameters at the existing head LR (1e-3) with the same per-step cosine anneal -- the champion's trunk-vs-head differential LR split is removed because there is no pretrained trunk left to protect; a new freeze_quantized_weights step runs after the epoch loop and before calibration/export, snapping every QAT module's weight to its quantized value in place

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: same loss formula as champion (Gaussian-smoothed cross-entropy against the field + expected-coordinate L2 + confidence BCE), computed against the new single field head's logits under live weight fake-quantization

implementation_brief:
model/model.py: (1) Delete `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, `_build_pretrained_trunk`, `PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH`, `IMAGENET_MEAN`, `IMAGENET_STD`, and the `norm_mean`/`norm_std` buffers and their use in forward() -- no ImageNet identifiers, constructors, or weight files may remain anywhere in model/ (backbonecheck.py scans stripped-of-docstrings code + bare filenames; this includes not reusing the filename mnv3s_features8.pt for anything). Replace the removed normalization with a simple fixed `(x - 0.5)` input shift (no learned/external stats). (2) Add two small wrapper modules: `QATConv2d(nn.Module)` wrapping a `nn.Conv2d`-equivalent weight/bias Parameter pair (support stride/padding/groups as needed) and `QATLinear(nn.Module)` wrapping a Linear weight/bias pair. Both store a `frozen_quantized: bool` instance attribute (default False, not a buffer -- it only gates which forward path runs, not model state) and a helper `_fake_quantize(w)`: per-output-channel symmetric INT8 STE, `scale = w.detach().abs().amax(dim=tuple(range(1, w.dim())), keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8) / 127.0`; `w_q = (w / scale).round().clamp(-127, 127) * scale`; return `w + (w_q - w).detach()`. forward(): if `frozen_quantized` is False, compute `w = self._fake_quantize(self.weight)` and run the conv/linear with `w`; if True, run directly with `self.weight` (already snapped in place, no rounding math emitted into the traced graph). Bias stays plain FP32, never quantized. (3) Build `_build_scratch_trunk()`: 5 sequential QATConv2d+BatchNorm2d+ReLU6 stages, channels 3->32 (stem, stride 2) -> 64 (stride 2) -> 128 (stride 2) -> 192 (stride 2) -> 224 (stride 1), all kernel_size=3 padding=1; 128x128 input -> 8x8x224 output. This is a target shape, not a hard requirement -- keep total conv params in the ~700k-1.0M range (verify with a quick param count before training). (4) `TinyLocNet.__init__`: trunk = the new scratch trunk; a FiLM generator `nn.Sequential(QATLinear(1, 16), nn.ReLU(), QATLinear(16, 2 * feat_ch))` producing gamma/beta from raw mean luminance (same `lum = x.mean(dim=(1,2,3))` input the champion's gate already computes); a `layout_squeeze` QATConv2d(224, 16, 1); a single `loc_logits = QATLinear(224 + 16*8*8, grid_k*grid_k)` (delete `dark_logits` and `gate` entirely -- no second head, no blend); `conf_head` rebuilt as a small QATLinear MLP over `[detached 224-d GAP, peak, ent, gap]` (same 4-input shape/semantics as champion's conf_head, just re-dimensioned). Keep `conf_shift` buffer, `cell_u`/`cell_v` buffers, `GRID_K`/`TARGET_SIGMA_CELLS`/`DECODE_BETA`/`GOOD_ERR_UV` constants exactly as-is (grid stays 32x32 -- this experiment is not testing grid resolution). (5) `forward()`: run `_c4_stack` as today; apply the FiLM gamma/beta to the trunk's raw feature map (`fmap = fmap * (1 + gamma.view(-1, C, 1, 1)) + beta.view(-1, C, 1, 1)`, gamma/beta computed once per (non-stacked) input then repeated 4x to match the C4 stack, matching how `lum4` is already repeated today) before GAP/layout-squeeze/loc_logits; compute the sharpened field per rotation view (do NOT collapse logits to one mean first), take each view's own peak mass as its ensemble weight, and produce the final logits as a peak-mass-weighted average of the 4 views' logits (normalize the 4 weights to sum to 1 per example) instead of champion's plain `.mean(dim=0)`; everything downstream (softmax decode, expected-coordinate soft-argmax, unsharpened-decode gap, confidence) keeps the champion's exact math, just reading the new logits/descriptor. (6) Add `freeze_quantized_weights(model)`: iterate `model.modules()`, for every `QATConv2d`/`QATLinear` call `_fake_quantize` on the live weight and assign the result back to `.weight.data` (no_grad), then set `.frozen_quantized = True`. `export_onnx()` itself is unchanged (still a plain `torch.onnx.export` call on a model already in this frozen state). (7) Restate the frozen contract untouched: `estimate_position()`'s signature, the ONNX I/O shapes (1x3x128x128 float32 [0,1] in, [[u, v, conf]] out), and `loss_fn`'s signature all stay exactly as today.

model/train.py: (1) In `train_area()`, replace the two-group optimizer (`trunk_params` at 1e-4 / `head_params` at 1e-3) with a single `torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)` plus the same `CosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max=total_steps, eta_min=0.0)` -- delete the now-meaningless `trunk_params`/`trunk_ids`/`head_params` split. (2) Immediately after the epoch loop ends and before `cal = calibrate_conf_shift(...)`, call `model.model.freeze_quantized_weights(model)` (import it from `model.model`) so calibration and export both run against the exact snapped weights that will ship. (3) After `export_onnx(model.cpu(), str(onnx_path))`, add the INT8 packing step: rename the just-written file to `models_dir / f'{area}_fp32.onnx'`, then `from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic, QuantType; quantize_dynamic(str(fp32_path), str(onnx_path), weight_type=QuantType.QInt8, op_types_to_quantize=['Conv', 'MatMul', 'Gemm'])` so `onnx_path` (the exact `models/{area}.onnx` path the frozen scorer reads) ends up holding the final INT8-packed model; the `_fp32.onnx` sibling is left on disk as a debug artifact only (not read by the scorer). `info['onnx_bytes']` (already reading `onnx_path.stat().st_size` after this point) will then correctly report the final shipped size -- verify it clears `MODEL_MAX_BYTES` (4,194,304) with real margin before considering the round healthy. Update `info['init']` to `'from-scratch (QAT int8 weight-only, dynamic-quantized at export)'`. (4) Leave `CAL_CROPS_PER_BUCKET`, `MIN_KEEP_RATE`, `TRAIN_REALIZATIONS`, `EPOCH_MULT`, `CONFUSABILITY_ALPHA`, `NEIGHBOR_EXCLUDE_R`, `compute_cell_weights()`, `prepare_realizations()`, `sample_epoch()`, `calibrate_conf_shift()`, and the CLI (`--area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed`) completely untouched -- every other stage of the training procedure and data strategy is out of scope for this experiment.
